source: NCERT Class XII, Introductory Microeconomics, Ch. 4 (The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition).

sections.heading: 1. Perfect Competition — Features

sub: **Many buyers and sellers** (each too small to affect price).

points: As a result, the firm is a **'price taker'** — it accepts the market price (set by industry demand and supply).

sections.heading: 2. Revenue Concepts
points: **Total Revenue (TR) = Price × Quantity**.
**Average Revenue (AR) = TR/Quantity = Price**.
**Marginal Revenue (MR) = ΔTR/ΔQuantity**.
Under perfect competition, **Price = AR = MR** (a horizontal demand curve for the firm).

sections.heading: 3. Firm's Equilibrium (Profit Maximisation)
points: A firm maximises profit where **MR = MC** (and MC is rising).
Since P = MR here, the condition is **Price = MC (MC rising)**.
**Profit** = TR − TC; earned when **AR > AC**; **normal profit** when AR = AC; **loss** when AR < AC.

sections.heading: 4. Shut-Down and Break-Even Points
points: **Break-even point** — where **P = AC** (only normal profit).
**Shut-down point** — where **P = minimum AVC**; below this the firm shuts down in the short run (cannot cover variable costs).
The firm's **short-run supply curve** = the rising part of its MC curve **above minimum AVC**.
In the **long run**, free entry/exit ensures firms earn only **normal profit (P = minimum LAC)**.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Perfect competition: many sellers, homogeneous product, free entry/exit, perfect knowledge; firm = price taker.
Price = AR = MR (horizontal firm demand curve).
Profit maximisation: MR = MC (MC rising) → P = MC.
Break-even: P = AC; Shut-down: P = minimum AVC.
Long-run: firms earn only normal profit (free entry/exit).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: In perfect competition, the firm is a **price taker**; **P = AR = MR**.
**Profit maximisation at MR = MC (with MC rising)**.
**Shut-down point = minimum AVC**; **break-even = minimum AC**.
In the **long run**, competitive firms earn only **normal profit**.
